good_thing: (Bourne, Massachusetts): Emergency crews and wildlife staff rescued a young raccoon whose head was stuck in a storm-drain grate. They brought the animal, grate included, to Cape Wildlife Center, where veterinary staff sedated it and used canola oil and plastic bags to ease it free. The raccoon was able to move its neck and limbs afterward and went to an outdoor enclosure for monitoring.
current_or_history: In 1932, Amelia Earhart took off from Los Angeles on a nonstop flight across the United States. She reached Newark the next day after 2,477 miles and 19 hours, 5 minutes, becoming the first woman to make the trip nonstop. About 150 people were waiting at the airport.
tiny_fact: Snapping shrimp close a claw so fast that it makes a tiny bubble. When the bubble pops, it can reach 218 decibels, helping the shrimp stun prey.
thought: You do not have to solve the whole week before giving today a decent start.
